bcn_001: You can recognise it by the trunk, 2.7 metres round, under a crown as wide as the tree is tall, 22 metres each way. It stands in the small public garden behind the surviving facades of the Casetes de l'Encarnacio.
bcn_002: You can recognise it by the sloped stone columns of Gaudi's viaduct built around it, the one living trunk inside a colonnade made to look like trees. It stands on the Carretera del Carmel side of Park Guell.
bcn_003: You can recognise it by the slim young trunk, about 90 centimetres round, standing inside the twisted dead wood of the four metre carob it regrew from. It stands by the Placa de la Natura in Park Guell.
bcn_005: You can recognise it by its height, roughly 40 metres and the biggest tree in the city, and by being the only wingnut recorded in Barcelona. It stands at the bottom of the Sot de l'Estany, the old quarry pit in the botanical garden.
bcn_006: You can recognise it by the trunk, 3.2 metres round under 24 metres of height, on an American swamp ash almost nobody plants here. It stands in the same Sot de l'Estany ravine as the garden's much taller wingnut.
bcn_007: You can recognise it by the crown, over 15 metres across on a tree only 12 metres tall, wide enough to shade a small plaza by itself. It stands in the Jardins de la Maternitat, probably the largest magnolia in the city.
bcn_009: You can recognise it by the rippled, root-like folds of the trunk, two and a half metres round at chest height on a tree 9.5 metres tall. It stands in Placa de Prim, one of the three ombus that give the square its character.
bcn_010: You can recognise them by four fan palms standing together in one enclosed courtyard, planted around 1904. They stand in the old Casa de la Misericordia, reached from Carrer d'Elisabets or through La Central bookshop.
bcn_011: You can recognise it by what looks like a pine and is not: drooping grey green jointed twigs, and two trunks fused at the base that split about 90 centimetres up to a combined five metres round. It stands facing the Cascada.
bcn_012: You can recognise it by the leaves, leathery and plain edged with none of an oak's lobes, and by the leaning stem that throws an 11 metre crown sideways, low enough to put a hand on. It stands on the sand near the Ciutadella bandstand.
bcn_013: You can recognise it in late autumn by the fruit on the path, grapefruit sized, yellow green and folded like a brain. It stands beside the Ciutadella lake, on a trunk about two and a half metres round.
bcn_014: You can recognise it by the pale straight trunk, about three metres round and bare a long way up before the crown begins, close to 30 metres tall. It stands inside the Casa de la Caritat grounds, in full view from Placa de les Caramelles.
bcn_016: You can recognise it by an ullastre, the low scrubby wild olive, grown into a proper tree of 14 to 17 metres with a crown over 13 metres wide. It stands above a retaining wall in the east sector of Park Guell.
bcn_017: You can recognise it by the thousands of pink mallow flowers that fill the whole crown once a year, fifteen metres up, and by the trunk 2.4 metres round. It stands to the left of the Teatre Grec amphitheatre, below the restaurant terrace.
bcn_019: You can recognise it by the crown, twenty metres wide over a walkway barely three metres across, so the path runs underneath it. It stands on the path linking the Teatre Grec and Laribal gardens, leaning out over the slope.
bcn_020: You can recognise it by the trunk, 3.3 metres round and possibly the thickest tipu tree in the city, under a crown 23 metres across. It stands in Placa de Carles Buigas at the foot of Montjuic, a few steps from the Magic Fountain.
bcn_023: You can recognise it by the flat umbrella crown on a trunk three and a half metres round, standing alone in open meadow rather than among other trees. It stands beside the palace, next to a sculpted female figure.
bcn_024: You can recognise them by the drooping leader shoots and branches sweeping down nearly to the grass, a group of 23 cedars rather than one trunk. They stand near the entrance of the Pedralbes gardens, the tallest about 25 metres.
bcn_025: You can recognise it by foliage in small jointed, scaled sprays and four valved woody cones closer to hardware than to a pine cone. It stands in the Pedralbes gardens on a trunk 1.2 metres round, shorter than nearly everything around it.
bcn_026: You can recognise them by the pair of them, two stone pines 21 metres tall on trunks 3.6 metres round. They stand in the Torre Girona gardens beside the old chapel that now holds the MareNostrum supercomputer in a glass box.
bcn_027: You can recognise it by its height, 23 metres and the tallest of the three protected trees here, on a trunk 2.9 metres round. It stands on the slope beside the ornamental pond and its viewpoint in the Torre Girona gardens.
bcn_028: You can recognise it by the trunk swelling at the base into a bottle shape, 2.5 metres round on a tree 22 metres tall. It stands halfway into the wooded part of the Torre Girona gardens, off the obvious route.
bcn_029: You can recognise it by the shape, 26 metres tall and 26 metres across on a trunk three and a half metres round, a plane nobody has ever cut back. It stands on open lawn in the Vil.la Amelia gardens.
bcn_030: You can recognise it by the bark hanging off in long ribbons over the smooth grey white surface underneath, and by the trunk, 5.2 metres round on a tree only 18 metres tall. It stands in the Vil.la Amelia gardens, the thickest trunk there.
bcn_031: You can recognise it by the fine weeping sprays of foliage that move in any wind at all, and by the clusters of pink berries that hang on from autumn into winter. It stands 12 metres tall on a 2.7 metre trunk in the Vil.la Amelia gardens.
bcn_032: You can recognise them by the double row flanking the main avenue like a colonnade with the path down the middle, 19 metres tall. They stand in the Vil.la Amelia gardens; the register counts fourteen, the garden's chronicler fifteen.
bcn_033: You can recognise it by two main limbs running out nearly horizontal, one of them resting on the ground, spreading a canopy from a base no wider than a doorway. It stands on the shared path beside the Hort de l'Avi allotments.
bcn_036: You can recognise it by the crown, 24 metres across on a tree 25 metres tall, unpruned where the city's other planes are cut back to knuckles each winter. It stands between the Ciutadella lake and the zoo fence.
bcn_037: You can recognise it by a single trunk 1.55 metres round on a plant usually clipped into a waist high hedge, under a crown six metres wide. It stands in front of the Glorieta de la Transsexual Sonia, the park's old bandstand.
bcn_039: You can recognise it by the leaves, cut far more deeply into narrow lobes than the hybrid planes on every street around it, and by its lower, looser shape. It stands in Placa de la Universitat in front of the university's main building.
bcn_040: You can recognise it by the height, 17 metres of avocado on a trunk only 80 centimetres round, gone straight up where a picked orchard tree is kept low and wide. It stands in Placa de Can Bruixa in Les Corts.
bcn_045: You can recognise it in autumn by the flat butter yellow it turns over about a fortnight before dropping almost all at once. It stands 17 metres tall on a trunk 1.4 metres round in the terraced bulb garden on the Montjuic hillside.
bcn_046: You can recognise it by the shape, twice as wide as it is tall: five metres high, a crown ten metres across and one trunk 1.8 metres round. It stands in Placa de Joanic, a single tree rather than the group of three trunks.
bcn_047: You can recognise it by its height, about 32 metres, and by trunk figures that disagree, 4.1 metres in the register against 2.4 measured in 2017. It stands alone among paths lined with 30 illuminated panels of the Declaration.
bcn_048: You can recognise it by the broad crown, 20 metres across on a trunk 2.9 metres round, the smaller of the garden's two catalogued trees. It stands about 130 metres from the much taller silky oak in the Jardins dels Drets Humans.
bcn_049: You can recognise it as the one broad leaved tree in a garden of cacti and succulents, three metres round under a crown spreading 20 metres. It stands on the terraces of the Jardins de Mossen Costa i Llobera.
bcn_050: You can recognise it by a yucca grown to 12 metres on a trunk 1.6 metres round, tree sized where most people expect a shrub. It stands on the seaward side of the path at the foot of the Miramar steps.
bcn_051: You can recognise it by the canopy, 15 metres across on a trunk 1.6 metres round, far wider than an avocado tree is usually allowed to grow. It stands on Placa Margarida Xirgu in front of the Teatre Lliure entrance.
bcn_052: You can recognise it by being the only thing on the street worth looking at, 20 metres tall on a trunk 2.3 metres round, with cream white flower clusters in late summer. It stands on Carrer de la Guardia Urbana in Poble-sec.
bcn_053: You can recognise it as the horse chestnut rather than the square's much thicker tipu tree, 15.5 metres tall on a trunk 1.84 metres round under an 11 metre crown. It stands in Placa de Carles Buigas beside the Font Magica.
bcn_054: You can recognise them by three trunks flowering together in the second half of April, magenta straight out of the bark before a leaf shows, crowns up to ten metres and the widest trunk 1.65 metres round. They stand in Placa Joanic.
bcn_059: You can recognise them by a double row of trunks grown thoroughly into the surrounding woodland, and by the big wrinkled inedible fruit the trees drop. They stand in the wooded part of the Torre Girona gardens, fourteen catalogued as one.
